title: Supported integral lattice Hom as a reduction tower
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with ring of integers $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi_E$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes are separated of finite type over $k$ and all morphisms are over $k$. On each small pro-étale site put $R_Y=p_Y^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$, $A_n=\mathcal O_E/(\pi_E^n)$ and $A_{n,Y}=p_Y^*\underline{A_n}$ for $n\ge1$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, def-sfb-torsion-stratum-coefficients]. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], in universes making these sites small [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $\operatorname{Res}_n:D(A_{n,X})\to D(R_X)$ for termwise restriction along the quotient coefficient morphism [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be closed, $j:V\hookrightarrow X$ its open complement, $u:S\hookrightarrow Z$ open and $a=i\circ u$. Use $a_!=i_*u_!$, closed module direct image after open module extension by zero [def-sfb-module-lower-star, def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek]. Let $L_0$ be a lisse $R_S$-module, meaning pro-étale locally finite free, and put $Q=a_!L_0$ and $L_0^\vee=\mathcal Hom_{R_S}(L_0,R_S)$ [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. Use the derived support functor $R\underline\Gamma_{Z,R}$ and global derived Hom of [sk-lem-formal-closed-support], the ordinary derived tensor of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], and derived global sections $R\Gamma$ [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology].

Let $v:T\hookrightarrow B$ be open, $h:B\hookrightarrow X$ closed, $b=h\circ v$, and $M_0$ a lisse $R_T$-module. Put $N=b_!M_0$, $\overline N_n=b_!(M_0/\pi_E^n)$ in $D(A_{n,X})$ and $N_n=\operatorname{Res}_n\overline N_n$. Give $(N_n)$ its quotient transitions. Define
$$T_R(K)=L_0^\vee\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{R_S}u^*R\underline\Gamma_{Z,R}K,\qquad F=T_R(N),\quad F_n=T_R(N_n),\quad B_n=R\Gamma(S,F_n)\in D(\operatorname{Ab}),$$
where the last expression forgets the coefficient action. Then $L_0^\vee$ is finite locally free; $N$ is derived complete [sk-def-pe-derived-completion], with $N_n\simeq\operatorname{Res}_n(N\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{R_X}A_{n,X})$ compatible with quotient transitions; and
$$N\simeq R\varprojlim_{n\ge1}N_n,\qquad F\simeq R\varprojlim_{n\ge1}F_n.$$
Here derived limits mean objects with their Roos triangles [def-weil-derived-limit]. Applying $T_R$ to the reduction Roos triangle gives a Roos triangle for $(F_n)$, and applying $R\Gamma(S,-)$ gives one for $(B_n)$. The support-Hom identifications give
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_{R_X}(Q,N)\simeq R\Gamma(S,F)\simeq R\varprojlim_{n\ge1}B_n,\qquad R\operatorname{Hom}_{R_X}(Q,N_n)\simeq B_n.$$
In particular, for every integer $q$,
$$\Ext^q_{R_X}(Q,N)\cong H^q(R\varprojlim_nB_n),\qquad H^q(B_n)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R_X)}(Q,N_n[q]),$$
where $\Ext^q(A,K)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R_X)}(A,K[q])$.

proof.text: First check the finiteness needed for extension by zero and closed direct image. By the finite-type definition each scheme in the statement has a finite affine cover by spectra of finitely generated $k$-algebras. The affine Noetherian lemma makes the closed-subset descending-chain condition hold on each member of this finite cover; a descending chain therefore stabilizes globally by taking the maximum of the finitely many stabilization indices. Every subset of such a Noetherian space is quasi-compact. In particular $X,Z,B$ are qcqs (intersections of affine opens are quasi-compact), and $j,u,v$ and the open complements of $i,h$ are quasi-compact: the inverse image of any affine open is a subset of a Noetherian space. Thus all uses below of the pro-étale open/closed lemmas satisfy their quasi-compactness hypotheses.

On a pro-étale trivializing cover $L_0$ is $R_S^{\oplus r}$. Its sheaf dual has the dual basis, hence is $R_S^{\oplus r}$ on that cover. Evaluation and the basis coevaluation satisfy the two triangular identities by $e_i^\vee(e_j)=\delta_{ij}$ and glue because evaluation is intrinsic. In particular $L_0$ is finite locally projective and $L_0^\vee$ is finite locally free, including rank zero. This verifies the source hypothesis of the support-Hom formula and the tensor hypothesis of the limit-preservation lemma.

Use the coefficient comparison $R_Y\cong\varprojlim_n A_{n,Y}$, with its actual quotient projections. The completed-coefficient free-resolution lemma then gives $[R_Y\xrightarrow{\pi_E^n}R_Y]\to\operatorname{Res}_n A_{n,Y}$ in degrees $-1,0$, K-flat and a quasi-isomorphism. On a cover where $M_0\cong R_T^{\oplus r}$ its tensor with $M_0$ is the direct sum of $r$ copies of this resolution. Thus $\pi_E^n:M_0\to M_0$ is injective, its cokernel is $M_0/\pi_E^n$, and $M_0\otimes^L_{R_T}A_{n,T}\cong M_0/\pi_E^n$ in $D(A_{n,T})$. The augmentation is the quotient map. Local isomorphisms here identify intrinsic quotient maps, so they glue.

The canonical map $M_0\to\varprojlim_n M_0/\pi_E^n$ is an isomorphism of sheaves. Indeed restriction to a slice is evaluation on its objects, so it preserves sheaf limits. On each trivializing slice this map is the finite direct sum of the coefficient isomorphism $R_T\cong\varprojlim_n A_{n,T}$ from the previous step; finite direct sums are finite products and commute with limits. Isomorphisms of sheaves are local, so the map is globally invertible. This argument allows locally varying ranks and does not commute stalks with infinite products. Each quotient transition is an epimorphism, since it is the factorization of the quotient $M_0\to M_0/\pi_E^n$ through $M_0/\pi_E^{n+1}$.

For the coefficients $R$, the module open/closed theorem makes $v_!$ and $h_*$ additive exact functors; the Cartesian coefficient isomorphisms identify their inverse-image coefficient rings with $R_T,R_B$. Applying $b_!=h_*v_!$ to the exact sequence $0\to M_0\xrightarrow{\pi_E^n}M_0\to M_0/\pi_E^n\to0$ gives $0\to N\xrightarrow{\pi_E^n}N\to N_n\to0$ on underlying $R_X$-modules. The action on its last term factors through $A_{n,X}$; it is exactly the scalar restriction of $b_!(M_0/\pi_E^n)$, since applying the same open/closed sheaf functors retains this quotient action. Using the K-flat resolution of $A_{n,X}$ from step 3, the derived reduction of $N$ is $[N\xrightarrow{\pi_E^n}N]$. Its augmentation to $N_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Hence $N_n\simeq\operatorname{Res}_n(N\otimes^L_{R_X}A_{n,X})$. For $n+1\to n$ the chain map is multiplication by $\pi_E$ in degree $-1$ and identity in degree $0$; its augmentation is the quotient $N_{n+1}\to N_n$. These comparisons are therefore compatible with all quotient transitions.

On module sheaves $v_!$ preserves products by the pro-étale extension-zero limit lemma; as an exact additive functor it preserves kernels, hence inverse limits of sequences (the limit is the kernel of $1-s$ on the product). The module adjunction $h^*\dashv h_*$ and preservation of limits by right adjoints give the same property for $h_*$. Consequently applying $h_*v_!$ to the canonical sheaf limit in step 4 gives $N\cong\varprojlim_n N_n$, through the specified quotient projections. Exactness from step 5 makes the transitions $N_{n+1}\to N_n$ epimorphic.

source.place: Lattices: exact extension by zero preserving limits (Stacks 09BP), and exact closed direct image (09BM) preserving limits as a right adjoint

proof.text: Apply the surjective-tower theorem on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with ring sheaf $R_X$ to the sheaves $N_n$. Its hypothesis is exactly the epimorphic quotient transitions established above. It identifies their sheaf product with their product in $D(R_X)$ and gives the distinguished Roos triangle $N\to\prod_nN_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_nN_n\to N[1]$, using the projections of step 6. Thus $N\simeq R\varprojlim_nN_n$. With the reduction identifications of step 5, this is the canonical completion map of the derived-completeness definition. In particular $N$ is derived complete, with the requested reduction tower.

proof.text: For $\Lambda=\underline{\mathcal O_E}$, the closed-support limit lemma applies to $u^*R\underline\Gamma_{Z,R}$ and to tensor with the finite locally free $L_0^\vee$ of step 2. Its statement specifies commutation by applying these functors to a Roos triangle. Apply the first functor and then the second to the Roos triangle in step 7. Their composites take $N,N_n$ to $F,F_n$, and identify the images of both products with $\prod_nF_n$. The maps between products are $1-s_F$: their $n$th coordinates are $\mathrm{pr}_n-T_R(N_{n+1}\to N_n)\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}$, because the additive functors preserve subtraction and the cited product comparisons preserve projections. This proves the asserted Roos triangle for $(F_n)$ and $F\simeq R\varprojlim_nF_n$.

source.place: Integral targets: the functors forming F commute with derived inverse limits of sequences

proof.text: Apply the ringed-site derived-sections limit theorem to the small pro-étale site of $S$, ring $R_S$, and its final object $S\to S$. It identifies $R\Gamma(S,\prod_nF_n)$ with $\prod_n R\Gamma(S,F_n)$ through the actual projection maps and sends the triangle of step 8 to a Roos triangle in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$. With $B_n=R\Gamma(S,F_n)$ this yields $R\Gamma(S,F)\simeq R\varprojlim_n B_n$, with quotient-induced transitions and with the coefficient action forgotten, exactly as stated. The indexing $n\ge1$ is the reindexing $n=m+1$ of its $m\ge0$ convention.

Use the supported stratum-Hom theorem with coefficient $\underline{\mathcal O_E}$, $a=i\circ u$ and the finite locally projective $L_0$ from step 2. Its quasi-compact complementary-open hypothesis was checked in step 1. At $K=N$ it gives $R\operatorname{Hom}_{R_X}(Q,N)\simeq R\Gamma(S,F)$, and at $K=N_n$ it gives $R\operatorname{Hom}_{R_X}(Q,N_n)\simeq B_n$. Its termwise-tensor convention agrees with derived tensor for this dual, as its statement specifies. Compose the first identification with step 9. Finally the theorem's shifted-Hom formula, first at $N$ and then at each $N_n$, gives $\Ext^q_{R_X}(Q,N)\cong H^q(R\varprojlim_nB_n)$ and $H^q(B_n)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R_X)}(Q,N_n[q])$ for every integer $q$, including negative $q$. All identifications of supported Hom are natural in the target by the cited statement.
